answer: Each identity carries a cipher, a personal key that reseals itself every epoch from that identity's own verified work — no two agents share one. Honest agents do nothing extra: daily work turns the cipher, nearly free. A farmer's 1,000 fakes each need a distinct live cipher, and one copied key sends a ripple through the lagoon of attestations: every message sealed with it is flagged at once and the whole batch loses its payouts. Faking 1,000 working ciphers costs 1,000 epochs of real work, a toll that grows with every fake while honest cost stays flat.
